name: Orchids — 60 by habit and region
notes: Kew accepts ~28,000 orchid species, so this is a curated set: tropical epiphytes (moth, vanda, dendrobium, cattleya, bucket, Darwin's), cloud-forest miniatures (masdevallia, dracula), savanna and desert orchids, the northern bog and fen orchids, European chalk-grassland mimics (bee, fly, lizard), the leafless ones that live entirely on fungi (bird's-nest, coralroot, the European ghost orchid), Australian heath oddities, and the great cliff clumps. Rules they add: dust seed on the wind that germinates only where the right fungus already lives (reads the fungi ledger), and most need one specific pollinator — the orchid is the plant that tells you whether the food web is whole. Some blooms are weather-gated (pigeon orchid 9 days after a storm; sun orchid only in full sun).
